newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut, Solidere B rise.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut, Solidere B rise.

text.p: Bank of Beirut hit a new high on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday and Solidere B shares broke an eight-week high amid strong demand.
Solidere B rose to $12 and Solidere A held steady at $11.5 after reaching their highest levels in eight weeks on Tuesday.
The LIBX bank index climbed 0.47 percent to 178.17. The LISPI general index rose 0.52 percent tp 92.61 and the BLOM general index increased 1.37 percent to 1017.83.
Total market turnover fell to 373,364 shares from 434,679 for a value of $4,586,340 against $5,113,737.
Solidere B's performance was the second time the stock had hit $12 since early January.
"Solidere shares have developed a strong upward momentum...high demand will not let the shares fall below $11.5," said a broker who requested anonymity.
Bank of Beirut rose to $4.43 from $4.375 in strong demand. Brokers last week predicted that BOB would reach as high as $4.5.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce held steady at a record high of $21. Banque Audi was also unchanged at a record $27.5.
The BSE said on Tuesday it was halting from July 14 block trading on the floor of the three listed banks in order to bring all deals into the central fixing system.
Of the four Industrial firms, only Ciment Libanais was traded, reaching $1.2812. It was last traded on July 2 at the same level.
There was no trade in Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic. -- Beirut editorial (9611) 745307 745308 602057
